newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier buys balance of de Havilland.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier buys balance of de Havilland.

text.p: Bombardier Inc. said on Tuesday that it completed the purchase of the 49 percent interest in de Havilland owned by the Province of Ontario for C$49 million.
Bombardier said it issued to Ontario a 15-year promissory note bearing interest of 7 percent with principal repayments of C$4.9 million to be made at the end of each of of years 6 through 15.

The transaction includes a covenant to operate the de Havilland business with a view to continuing aircraft final assembly, participation in Bombardier's aerospace programs and diversification of activities while maintaining engineering capability, investment in plant and equipment and provision of opportunities to Canadian suppliers.

Bombardier and the Government of Ontario purchased the business and assets of Boeing Co's de Havilland Division on January 22, 1992. For that transaction, Bombardier provided 51 percent and Ontario 49 percent of C$100 million of equity in a newly-created company, de Havilland Holdings Inc.
Bombardier had the right to buy, and Ontario the right to sell to Bombardier, from February 1, 1996 to January 31, 1997, all of Ontario's interest in de Havilland for C$49 million.
